evidence.claim: The nomination describes farmsteads whose arrangement responds to the landforms, contrasting that pattern with the more regular terrain and intensive horse-farm development elsewhere in rural Fayette County.
evidence.quote: features whose spatial organization is very influenced by the desiccated landforms around it. This contrasts with the rest of rural Fayette County, which has been more intensively developed, especially for horse farms, and is much more regular topographically.

evidence.claim: The nomination also notes newer barns and houses that follow traditional choices of building sites and scale.
evidence.quote: The new development in the district tends to perpetuate the traditional patterns in land use, choice of building sites, and scale.

flags: Cache documents the designation date but not its rationale, road construction, drive time, curves or grades. Overview is shorter and uses documented rural context.

Athens page gives incompatible settlement and charter dates. Its Daniel Boone fort claim (1775) also conflicts with Boone Station’s account of Israel Boone’s settlement (1776) and Daniel’s later residence. Those claims are omitted.
Grimes complex page opens with 1813 but dates the mill building to 1803. They may describe different components; construction year omitted pending primary documentation.
The current claim of continuous hunt occupancy since 1928 exceeds the evidence. Retained purchase and headquarters history without asserting uninterrupted use.
Historic district moment is a landscape context entry before the mill on the return leg, not an access point. No coordinate pin or private-property access is implied.
Official inventory alternates McCalls Mills Road and McCalls Mill Road. Copy uses the latter, matching the return-leg wording.
